title: A new node is checked against the nodes already on the board, not only against its own session
description:
Today `propose` and `open_node` check edges only inside the call: keys resolve to each other, `findCycle` runs, loose decisions are refused (packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts ~136-235, packages/mcp/src/tools/flag.ts `open_node`). Nothing compares a new node with what earlier sessions put on the board, and the planning agent has no way to: the `board` tool renders titles only, no files and no description. So a node planned today that must wait on (or must hold) a node from last week lands with no edge — e.g. a design node that should build on earlier design nodes.

Two halves, one node:
1. Mechanical. After the write, `propose` and `open_node` list every open (not accepted, not dismissed) node that shares a file glob with a new node and has no edge to it either way — id, title, the shared globs. Reuse `touches` from packages/core/src/team.ts (today `overlaps` there only looks at claimed nodes; add a sibling that looks at every open node, export it from packages/core/src/index.ts). It warns, it does not refuse: two nodes can share a file without one waiting on the other, and SOBER already warns about overlap at run time.
2. Semantic. plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md gets a step before `propose`: for each new node, name which existing nodes it must wait on and which existing nodes must now wait on it — same area, same design surface, same record or tool — and put the first in `dependsOn`; after `propose`, act on the overlap list and call `bind` for the second (passing the full existing `dependsOn`, since `bind` replaces it). Regenerate packages/*-plugin/skills/plan/SKILL.md with `pnpm plugins`.

Acceptance: an MCP test where a board holds node A with files X, a later `propose` adds B with files X and no edge, and the reply names A; the same with an edge present names nothing; the generated skills match the source (test/integration/plugin.test.ts).

brief.approach:
Score 6: a new core export with its test, two MCP tools changed, and a skill step regenerated to four hosts — three packages that have to land together, and the semantic half is prose that is easy to get vague.

**1. `core` gains one function, beside the one it is modelled on.** `packages/core/src/team.ts` already holds `touches` (a private glob-pair test, with its own `ponytail:` comment on what it deliberately misses) and `overlaps` at line 40, which walks every node and keeps the ones sharing a glob — but gates on `node.claim !== null || alsoStarting.includes(other)`, so it only ever sees nodes somebody has started. Add a sibling in the same file, `unlinked`, with the same `Overlap` return shape so nothing new is exported as a type:

```ts
export const unlinked = (nodes: ReadonlyMap<string, Node>, id: string): Overlap[]
```

Same walk, three differences: an "open" node is one with `accepted === null` and `dismissal === null` — started or not; skip the node itself; and skip any node already joined by an edge in either direction. For the edge test, `dependsOn` is the only edge on the record, so a pair is joined when `mine.dependsOn.includes(other) || node.dependsOn.includes(id)`. Do **not** reach for `between` from `graph.ts`: a transitive path is still a real connection and this warning is about a pair with no edge at all, which is the cheaper and more honest question. `by` stays on the result and is `node.claim?.by ?? null` as in `overlaps`. Sort by id, as `overlaps` does.

Export it from `packages/core/src/index.ts` beside `overlaps`, and update `packages/core/src/__snapshots__/exports.test.ts.snap` with `-u`. The ceiling in `exports.test.ts` is 107 and the surface is already over it; that prints a warning by design (ADR 0028) — do not raise the number.

Tests in `packages/core/src/team.test.ts`, which already tests `overlaps`: an unclaimed open node sharing a glob is found (this is the case `overlaps` misses and the whole reason for the function); a pair already joined by `dependsOn` in either direction is not; an accepted node is not; a dismissed node is not; a node with no shared glob is not.

**2. `propose` warns after the write — `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts`.** The handler writes decisions then nodes (`for (const [id, record] of records) await writeNode(...)`) and then builds `lines` for the reply. After the write, `loadBoard` again and call `unlinked` for each newly written id, collecting the results. Append to the reply, only when there is something to say, a block naming each new node and, under it, each open node it shares globs with — id, title, the shared globs. Close with the sentence that makes it actionable: these are not refusals, and an edge that belongs is added with `bind`, passing the node's full `dependsOn` because `bind` replaces the list rather than appending to it.

It warns and never refuses. Two nodes can share a file with neither waiting on the other, and SOBER already warns about the same overlap at run time — a refusal here would make a planning session unable to write a legitimate board.

**3. `open_node` in `packages/mcp/src/tools/flag.ts` gets the same block**, built from the same function and worded the same way. One node in, so the list is one heading; do not fork the rendering — write the renderer once in whichever of the two files is natural and import it, or keep it in `packages/mcp/src/render.ts` where `renderBoard` and `renderDecisions` already live. `render.ts` is the right home.

**4. The skill — `plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md`.** Step 4 is now "Decompose into nodes" (the plan skill was renumbered to eight steps by `the-plan-skill-asks-what-it-does-not-kno-7spu`, which landed; read the file rather than the numbers written here). Add to step 4, as a short paragraph, not a new numbered step: for each new node, name which nodes already on the board it must wait on, and which of them must now wait on it — same area, same design surface, same record or tool. The first goes in `dependsOn` in the `propose` call. The second cannot: `dependsOn` only points backwards, so after `propose` returns, read the overlap block it printed and call `bind` for each edge that belongs, passing the existing node's **full** `dependsOn` plus the new id, because `bind` replaces.

Say why this is possible now and was not before: the `board` tool renders titles only, so a planning agent had no way to see files or descriptions of earlier nodes — the overlap block is that missing information, delivered at the moment it is useful. Then `pnpm plugins` and commit the four generated copies; `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` is the drift check.

**5. Integration test** in `test/integration/mcp.test.ts`, the three cases the node's own text asks for: a board holding node A with files `X`; a later `propose` adding B with files `X` and no edge — the reply names A with the shared glob; the same `propose` with `dependsOn: ['A']` — the reply names nothing; and `open_node` with overlapping files gets the same block. Use the existing `board()` and `call()` helpers rather than a new fixture.

acceptance.proves: `unlinked` finds an unclaimed open node sharing a glob — the case `overlaps` is blind to — and stays quiet for a pair already joined by an edge, for an accepted node and for a dismissed one; and the new name is in the snapshot a reviewer reads

a propose that adds a node overlapping an existing one names it with the shared globs, and the same propose carrying the edge names nothing — the warning fires on the real gap and not on ordinary work
the four generated plan skills match the source after `pnpm plugins`, so the bind-afterwards instruction reaches every host

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'CEILING = 107' -- packages/core/src/exports.test.ts && git grep -q 'unlinked' -- packages/core/src/index.ts packages/core/src/team.ts
acceptance.proves: one function was added and exported, and the export ceiling was not raised to hide it
the change is core, the two MCP tools, the plan skill and its generated copies — no schema move, no CLI, no dashboard, no server route
the new export and both tool replies compile
